Generated 2026-07-09  ·  Revised 2026-08-17 (post-launch)  ·  Source: 5-module KB deep research, Anthropic T1 docs  ·  Scope: how Tag works, STA fit, rollout plan

Recommendation: ADOPT - pilot one channel now, build the server Tag-compatible

Bottom line: Claude Tag is a shared @Claude teammate inside Slack, included with STA's existing Team plan at no per-seat cost - channel work bills to an org usage balance, and Anthropic issued a launch credit STA can pilot on before spending anything. It is the lowest-friction way to put AI in front of the 9 staff who do not use Adam's Cowork system.

The architecture answer: Tag CAN consume a custom MCP server (confirmed in Anthropic's docs: a plugin declaring the server + a host credential). Build the STA company server Tag-compatible - one server then feeds Tag channels, Cowork, and personal DMs. Action: fund/verify the usage balance, stand up the #ask-claude pilot, and make the expansion call.

Status as of 2026-08-17: the new Tag experience launched 2026-08-03 and is in Team/Enterprise beta. The legacy Claude in Slack app is gone - Tag is the only version now, so the "decide before the cutover" window described in the original briefing has closed. The recommendation below is unchanged; the timeline has moved.

How it works: one shared Claude, invoked by tagging, acting under org-owned credentials

Tag @Claude in any channel it has been added to and it starts a working session in that thread - running asynchronously in an Anthropic-hosted sandbox, editing a visible checklist in place, and posting the result (a reply, a file, a chart, or a draft PR). Anyone in the channel can steer a running task just by replying. The architectural shift from the old personal Slack app: in channels, Claude acts as itself under service-account credentials an admin provisions, and its access follows the channel, not the person asking. DMs are the opposite - there Claude runs on your personal account with your own connectors, billed to your seat.

Context is now channel-wide, not per-message. The earlier model rebuilt context around each individual mention. Tag now works from the channel as a whole, which is why seeding channel memory deliberately (below) matters more than it used to - what the channel holds is what Claude reasons from, on every invocation, for everyone.

The load-bearing finding: your company server can plug straight into Tag

Confirmed · T1

Custom MCP servers are supported - via a plugin that declares the server, plus a credential for its host

Anthropic's docs confirm the pattern: attach a plugin whose .mcp.json points at the server URL, then add a credential (Bearer/OAuth) for the server's host on the bundle's Credentials tab. Auth is injected at Anthropic's Agent Proxy - the model never holds the key, and egress is default-deny. Two traps: a .mcp.json committed to a repo is NOT loaded (must ship as an attached plugin), and threads lock their config at start (updates reach new threads only).

What this means for the STA server build: expose a public HTTPS MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP per the MCP spec - transport not named explicitly in Tag docs, verify against a live endpoint during the pilot), use Bearer or OAuth mapped to a service account, ship it as a plugin bundled with STA-specific skills (for example the SMS 2.0 vs Qmlativ compatibility rules), and issue read-only vs write tokens in separate Access Bundles so a general channel gets read while a private ops channel gets write. One implementation then serves Tag, Cowork, and Claude.ai - build it Tag-compatible from day one.

The guardrails that matter for a K-12 vendor

  • Paste rule is the real exposure. Tag retains channel memory and transcripts (that is why ZDR orgs cannot use it). Staff rule: never paste student PII, credentials, or unreleased customer data into a Tag channel - use a DM. Team-plan data is not used for model training under Anthropic's Commercial Terms.
  • Removal does not delete data. Uninstalling, removing from a channel, or deleting a bundle leaves memory, standing instructions and transcripts in place - deletion uses the dedicated controls at claude.ai admin settings. The commonly repeated "30-day auto-delete on disconnect" claim is unverified for Tag.
  • Set spend before widening. Org cap + per-channel limits at claude.ai/admin-settings/usage/claude-tag; at the cap Claude stops and says so (never silently truncates). Per-user attribution does not exist - the channel is the unit, so map channels to teams.
  • Tune ambient per channel, never globally. Standing instructions run with the channel's credentials and are the documented token-burn risk; audit them org-wide from the Scheduled-work tab.
  • Set Members to "any organization member" so Slack guests cannot invoke Claude (per-role gating needs Enterprise); Claude stays disabled in guest channels by default.
  • Review memory monthly. Ask "@Claude what do you remember about this channel?" and prune - auto-accumulated memory is the top early-adopter opacity complaint. Seed it deliberately instead.

Rollout: the cutover has already happened, so the sequence is now un-dated

The original plan was paced against the legacy app's retirement. That date passed on 2026-08-03 and Tag is now the only version, so the steps below are sequenced by dependency rather than by calendar - each one gates the next, and the pilot still comes before any customer-facing channel.

Do these, in order

  1. Step 1 - admin setup: at claude.ai/admin-settings/claude-tag, run setup (Owner role), confirm the launch usage credit, set an org spend cap, and set Members to "any organization member." Keep the default "Slack default" bundle empty of credentials for now.
  2. Step 2 - pilot: create #ask-claude (test in a private channel first), invite @Claude, seed channel memory with the KB pointers and the "cite or route to a human" rule. No connectors yet - prove value on Slack content alone. Seeding matters more now that context is channel-wide.
  3. Step 3 - second channel + staff guidance: add the Behind the Bell channel. Publish the one-page staff guideline (invocation basics, paste rule, human-review rule, escalation) - the KB module has the full outline, ready for the Training Kit Hub.
  4. Step 4 - server build: lock the Tag-compatible architecture - public HTTPS MCP endpoint, Bearer/OAuth service-account auth, delivered as a plugin with STA skills. Re-verify the plugin mechanics and transport against live docs immediately before finalizing (still in beta - docs shift).
  5. Step 5 - customer-facing: connect the server + Help Center/Salesforce read access to #support via a dedicated read-only bundle; enforce the draft-until-human-sends rule; watch the per-channel spend breakdown for two weeks.
  6. Step 6 - then decide: sales/renewal channel, DM policy (on or off org-wide), and whether any standing instruction earns a per-channel spend cap. Review channel memory monthly from here on.
Beta caveat: Tag is still marked beta and behavior may change, so the KB module set stays on a monthly re-check cadence. The cutover is done - the new Tag experience launched 2026-08-03 and the legacy Claude in Slack app is retired, so there is no longer a deadline forcing the rollout call. Re-verify any mechanic in this briefing against live docs before you build on it.
